Super Typhoon Bavi will continue to move to the west-northwest and
away from the Marianas this evening. Trailing rain bands behind the
typhoon will continue to bring periods of numerous to widespread 
showers and isolated to scattered thunderstorms in the storm's wake.
Flooding impacts will be further exacerbated or new instances of 
flooding will be possible with additional heavy rainfall. Outer bands
from Bavi will continue to impact the islands into Tuesday with 
periods of heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms continuing 
through the day. Slightly drier weather will begin on Wednesday with 
shower chances dropping to lower-end scattered with thunderstorm 
chances continuing to decrease through Thursday. Shower coverage is 
expected to drop to isolated for all islands by Friday. Tropical 
storm force winds (sustained up to 58 mph) will continue for all 
islands through early Tuesday morning with conditions gradually 
improving through Tuesday, though quite breezy conditions will 
likely continue through much of the day. 

Marine/Surf...
Combined seas between 15 and 25 feet over coastal waters will
gradually decrease from east to west as Super Typhoon Bavi moves 
away. Tanapag buoy data shows that maximum wave heights exceeded 35 
feet as Bavi crossed the islands this morning. Altimetry data from 
this morning showed combined seas between 10 and 20 feet to the west
of Super Typhoon Bavi's approach, and to the east of its passage. 
As Bavi moves away to the west-northwest, dangerous surf up to 20 
feet remains possible, with surf levels increased along west and 
south facing reefs now that Bavi's center has moved west of the 
Marianas, and gradually easing along north and east reefs. As Bavi
moves away, south and west swells will prevail into the latter half
of the week, and surf is expected to remain hazardous along west-
facing reefs during this time, potentially into the end of this week.

Tropical Systems...
A Typhoon Warning remains in effect for the Marianas as Super Typhoon
Bavi (09W) moves away from the coastal waters. Himawari satellite 
imagery this afternoon shows Bavi's center at 15.0N 143.9E, about 
105 miles west-northwest of Rota, or 120 miles north-northwest of 
Guam. Earlier this morning, Bavi's eye made direct passage over 
Rota. Extreme Wind Warnings were issued, with catastrophic eyewall 
winds exceeding 150 mph impacting the entirety of the island,
starting from east to west at around 0700 ChST. Storm intensity at 
time of passage over Rota was 180 mph within the eyewall. For Guam, 
Tinian, and Saipan, typhoon conditions, including sustained wids of 
74 mph or greater, were verified. Now, damaging tropical storm 
conditions continue across the Marianas with occasional typhoon-force
gusts, but are gradually easing. Bavi is forecast to continue west- 
northwest at around 15 mph as a Category 5 Super Typhoon through 
Wednesday, with tropical storm conditions expected to depart the 
Marianas late tonight after midnight.

For more information on Super Typhoon Bavi, please refer to the 
Tropical Cyclone Public Advisory issued by the National Weather 
Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM and the Tropical Cyclone 
Warning issued by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO 
header WTPN31 PGTW.

Eastern Micronesia...
Mostly gentle winds across the region, with a few pockets of moderate
winds evident near weak troughs embedded in the trade-wind flow. the
two buoys near Majuro indicate seas of 4 ft. Higher seas are observed
across Kosrae and Pohnpei due to the combination of distant SE
groundswell from the southern hemisphere and swell from Super 
Typhoon Bavi and its monsoon tail.

Little change to the previous forecast. An overall uneventful pattern
is expected through the remainder of the week. A few disturbances
will ride westward on the gentle trades and the generally gentle
winds will occasionally shift, inducing episodes of showers when
moisture and convergence align. However, nothing too impactful is
expected other than a stray thunderstorm. Winds look to remain gentle
to moderate through the remainder of the week. A decent amount of the
southeast swell has been directed across the the region due to
distant storm activity northeast of New Zealand and closer to the
Solomons. This will mesh with swell from Bavi throughout the week,
creating some crossed-up seas near Kosrae and Pohnpei. These seas
don't appear to exceed 5 feet, but the opposing swells and crossed
nature is something to keep in mind.

Western Micronesia...
Observations from Chuuk Lagoon indicate the monsoon is easing and
shifting west. Seas remain elevated, prompting a continuation of the
Small Craft Advisory. Farther west, winds and seas have been 
building across Yap and Palau through the day as the monsoon inflow 
feeds Super Typhoon Bavi. Showers have yet to build in earnest over 
Palau and Yap, but the cirrus tufts tied to Bavi's outflow are 
drifting overhead Yap this afternoon.
